review: The hymn is Luke 15:11–32 (the prodigal son), so 1:4 quotes the father's command: שַׁחֲטוּ אֶת־עֵגֶל הַמַּרְבֵּק in the text, shortened to עֵגֶל מְפֻטָּם for the tune.
1:2 בֵּן תּוֹעֶה שָׁנִים — 'a son wandering for years'; the Arabic شَارِدًا ضَلَّ سِنِين is a participle plus verb, and Hebrew compresses it into a construct so the line stays at six.
2:3 חָיָה זֶה אֲשֶׁר־מֵת — Luke 15:24 (כִּי זֶה בְנִי הָיָה מֵת וַיֶּחִי); the Hebrew keeps the relative clause rather than the demonstrative alone.
3:1 יוֹדְעִים הַגְּדוּדִים — 'the hosts know'; the glossary fixes גְּדוּד for جُنْد, and the plural here is the heavenly host of Eph 3:10, which is what the Arabic الأَجْنَادُ means in this hymn.
4:4 הַנְּכוֹנָה — 'the right/true love'; the Arabic الصَّحِيح is 'sound, correct', and נָכוֹן is its biblical equivalent (Ps 51:12).
